headline: This law requires the Government Accountability Office to report on VA agreements with outside groups about suicide prevention and mental health care.
what_it_does: The Government Accountability Office, which is Congress's audit agency, must review and report on written agreements the Department of Veterans Affairs has signed with non-VA organizations. The agreements cover suicide prevention and providing or coordinating mental health services. The summary describes a reporting requirement and does not change how these agreements work.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who use VA mental health or suicide prevention services
who_it_affects.how: The law adds a government review of the outside partnerships that may help deliver their care, but it does not change their benefits or eligibility.
The department must make its agreements with non-VA entities on these topics available for the Government Accountability Office to report on.

who_it_affects.group: Non-VA organizations that sign agreements with the VA on mental health or suicide prevention
who_it_affects.how: Their agreements with the VA on these topics may be included in the government report.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on October 20, 2020. The summary does not give a due date for the Government Accountability Office report.
